title.en: Volume 124 Book of Later Zhou 26: Biographies 4 - Wang Yin, He Fejin, Liu Ci, Wang Jin, Shi Yanchao, Shi Yi, Wang Lingwen, Zhou Mi, Li Huaizong, Bai Wenke, Bai Yanyu, Tang Jinsi
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 周書15: 列傳四 王殷 何福進 劉詞 王進 史彥超 史懿 王令溫 周密 李懷忠 白文珂 白延遇 唐景思 Volume 124 Book of Later Zhou 26: Biographies 4 - Wang Yin, He Fejin, Liu Ci, Wang Jin, Shi Yanchao, Shi Yi, Wang Lingwen, Zhou Mi, Li Huaizong, Bai Wenke, Bai Yanyu, Tang Jinsi

sentences.zh: 王殷，瀛州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yin was a man of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin was a native of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖昌裔，本州別駕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Changyi was vice-prefect of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Changyi had served as vice-prefect of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖光，滄州教練使，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guang was training commissioner of Cang Prefecture and thereupon made his household there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guang was training commissioner of Cang Prefecture, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 唐末，幽、滄大亂，殷父鹹珪避地南遷，因投於魏軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, You and Cang were in great disorder; Yin's father Xian'gui fled south to escape the turmoil and thereupon joined the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang was collapsing, You and Cang fell into chaos; Yin's father Xian'gui fled south and enlisted with the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 殷自言生於魏州之開元寺，既長從軍，漸為偏將。

translations.literal: Yin himself said he was born at Kaiyuan Temple in Weizhou; once grown he followed the army and gradually became a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said he had been born at Kaiyuan Temple in Weizhou; when he came of age he entered military service and gradually rose to subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，為華州馬步軍副指揮使，因家於華下。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang reign, he was deputy commander of Huazhou's cavalry and infantry armies and thereupon made his household below Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tang Tongguang era he became deputy commander of Huazhou's combined horse and foot forces and established his household in the Hua region.

sentences.zh: 天成中，移授靈武都指揮使，久之代還。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was transferred and appointed commander of Lingwu; after a long time a replacement came and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng period he was reassigned as overall commander at Lingwu; after a long tour he was relieved and recalled.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，張令昭據鄴叛，殷從範延光討之，首冒矢石，率先登城，以功授祁州刺史，尋改原州。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, Zhang Lingzhao held Ye in rebellion; Yin followed Fan Yanguang to attack him, first braved arrows and stones, and was first to scale the wall; for his merit he was appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture, soon changed to Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingtai era Zhang Lingzhao seized Ye and rebelled; Yin followed Fan Yanguang against him, took the lead under fire, and was first over the wall. For this he was made prefect of Qi Prefecture, then soon transferred to Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 殷性謙謹好禮，事母以孝聞，每與人結交，過從皆先稟於母，母命不從，殷必不往，雖在軍旅，交遊不雜。

translations.literal: Yin's nature was modest, cautious, and fond of ritual propriety; his service to his mother was renowned for filial piety; whenever he formed friendships, every visit and association was first reported to his mother—if his mother's command was not followed, Yin would certainly not go; even while in the army, his social contacts were not indiscriminate.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was modest, careful, and devoted to propriety, and his filial devotion to his mother was well known. Whenever he made friends he asked his mother's leave before visiting them; if she forbade it he would not go. Even in camp his company was selective.

sentences.zh: 及為刺史，政事小有不佳，母察之，立殷於庭，詰責而杖之。

translations.literal: When he became prefect, if his administration had the slightest fault, his mother detected it, made Yin stand in the courtyard, questioned and rebuked him, and beat him with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became prefect, the least slip in his governance would be noticed by his mother. She would make him stand in the courtyard, rebuke him, and beat him with a staff.

translations.literal: (Annotation:
translations.idiomatic: (From the History of Ouyang:

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：殷為刺史，政事有小失，母責之，殷即取杖授婢仆，自笞於母前。）〉

translations.literal: (The History of Ouyang: When Yin was prefect, if his administration had a slight fault, his mother reproved him; Yin immediately took the staff and handed it to female servants, then flogged himself before his mother.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Ouyang Xiu records: When Yin was prefect, any small lapse brought his mother's rebuke; he would hand the rod to a servant and flog himself in her presence.)〉

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，丁內艱，尋有詔起復，授憲州刺史，殷上章辭曰：「臣為末將，出處無損益於國家。

translations.literal: In Jin's Tianfu era, he underwent mourning for his mother; soon there was an edict recalling him to office; he was appointed prefect of Xian Prefecture; Yin memorialized refusing, saying: "Your subject is a lowly general whose going or staying benefits or harms the state not at all.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin's Tianfu reign he entered mourning for his mother. Soon an edict recalled him to service and appointed him prefect of Xian, but Yin memorialized to decline: "Your servant is only a junior officer whose presence or absence neither helps nor harms the state.

sentences.zh: 臣本燕人，值鄉國離亂，少罹偏罰，因母鞠養訓導，方得成人，不忍遽釋苴麻，遠離廬墓，伏願許臣終母喪紀。

translations.literal: Your subject is originally a man of Yan; when my homeland was torn by disorder I narrowly suffered partial punishment; only through my mother's nurturing and instruction did I become a man; I cannot bear hastily to lay aside coarse hemp mourning and leave far from my parent's tomb; I humbly beg permission to complete the full mourning period for my mother.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of Yan. When my homeland was torn apart I barely escaped unjust punishment; only my mother's care and teaching made me a man. I cannot bear to cast off my mourning garb too soon and leave my mother's grave. I beg leave to complete the full mourning period."

sentences.zh: 」晉高祖嘉而許之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu of Jin commended him and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Jin praised him and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，會殷服闋，召典禁軍，累遷奉國右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi of Jin succeeded, as Yin's mourning ended he was summoned to command the palace guard, and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Right Wing of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi of Jin succeeded, Yin's mourning had ended and he was summoned to command the palace guard, rising eventually to commander of the Fengguo Army's right wing.

sentences.zh: 漢祖受命，從討杜重威於鄴下，殷與劉詞皆率先力戰，矢中於首，久之，出折鏃於口中，以是漢祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When the Han founder received the mandate, following the campaign against Du Chongwei below Ye, both Yin and Liu Ci fought at the forefront with all their strength; an arrow struck Yin's head, and after a long while he drew out the broken arrowhead from his mouth; for this the Han founder commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder took power, Yin joined the campaign against Du Chongwei below Ye. He and Liu Ci both fought at the front; an arrow struck Yin's head, and only after a long while did he spit out the broken tip. The Han founder commended him for this.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使，領夔州節度使，會契丹寇邊，遣殷領兵屯澶州。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou, he was transferred to commander of the Palace Guard Infantry and concurrently made military governor of Kuizhou; when the Khitan raided the border, Yin was sent to lead troops stationed at Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianyou he was made commander of the palace guard infantry and concurrently military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitan raided the frontier he was sent to hold Cangzhou with troops.

sentences.zh: 及李業等作亂，漢隱帝密詔澶帥李洪義遣圖殷，洪義懼不克，反以變告殷，殷與洪義同遣人至鄴，請太祖赴內難。

translations.literal: When Li Ye and others rebelled, the Hidden Emperor of Han secretly ordered Cangzhou commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin; Hongyi feared he could not succeed and instead informed Yin of the conspiracy; Yin and Hongyi together sent messengers to Ye requesting Taizu come to resolve the inner turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye and others rose in revolt, the Hidden Emperor secretly ordered Cangzhou commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin. Hongyi feared failure and instead warned Yin. Together they sent envoys to Ye asking Taizu to come and quell the court crisis.

sentences.zh: 殷從平京師，授侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yin followed in pacifying the capital and was appointed commander of the Palace Guard Imperial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yin followed in pacifying the capital and was appointed commander of the palace guard's imperial army.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，授天雄軍節度使，加同平章事，典軍如故。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, he was appointed military governor of the Tianxiong Army, given the added title of Co-Governor, and continued to command the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yin was made military governor of the Tianxiong army, given the added title of Co-Governor, and kept command of the guard as before.

sentences.zh: 殷赴鎮，以侍衛司局從，凡河北征鎮有戍兵處，鹹稟殷節制。

translations.literal: Yin went to his command; staff of the Palace Guard accompanied him; wherever garrison troops were stationed among the Hebei military prefectures, all reported to Yin's control.
translations.idiomatic: Yin went to his post with palace-guard staff in attendance, and every Hebei command that held garrison troops fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 又於民間多方聚斂，太祖聞而惡之，因使宣諭曰：「朕離鄴時，帑廩所儲不少，卿與國家同體，隨要取給，何患無財。

translations.literal: He also extensively extorted from the populace; Taizu heard and despised this, and sent an envoy to instruct him, saying: "When I left Ye, the treasury stores were not few; you and the state share the same body—take what you need whenever required—why fear lack of funds?".
translations.idiomatic: He also squeezed the people on many fronts. Taizu heard of it with disgust and sent word: "When I left Ye the treasuries were well stocked. You and the state are one body—take what you need whenever you need it. Why worry about money?".

sentences.zh: 」二年夏，太祖征兗還，殷迎謁於路，宴賜而去。

translations.literal: " In summer of the second year, as Taizu returned from campaigning at Yan, Yin met and paid respects on the road, received a feast and gifts, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That summer in the second year Taizu returned from the Yan campaign. Yin met him on the road, was feasted and rewarded, and then went home.

sentences.zh: 及王峻得罪，太祖遣其子飛龍使承誨往鄴，令口諭峻之過惡，以慰其心。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun fell into disgrace, Taizu sent his son the Feilong Commissioner Chenghui to Ye to orally convey Jun's faults and offenses, to comfort Yin's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun fell from favor, Taizu sent his son Commissioner Chenghui of Feilong to Ye to tell Yin of Jun's crimes by word of mouth and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，以永壽節上表請覲，太祖雖允其請，且慮殷之不誠，尋遣使止之。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year, on the Yongshou festival he memorialized requesting an audience; though Taizu granted the request, he also feared Yin's sincerity and soon sent an envoy to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the third year he memorialized for an audience on the Yongshou festival. Taizu granted the request but doubted his sincerity and soon sent an envoy to turn him back.

sentences.zh: 何福進在鎮州，素惡殷之太橫，福進入朝，摭其陰事以奏之，太祖遂疑之。

translations.literal: He Fujin was at Zhen Prefecture and had long hated Yin's overbearing conduct; Fujin entered court and gathered secret matters to memorialize; Taizu thus grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin at Zhenzhou had long resented Yin's arrogance. When Fujin came to court he collected secret reports against Yin, and Taizu grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以郊禋有日，殷自鎮入覲，太祖令依舊內外巡警。

translations.literal: That winter, as the suburban sacrifice drew near, Yin came from his command for audience; Taizu ordered patrol duties inside and outside as before.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, with the suburban sacrifice approaching, Yin came from his post for audience. Taizu restored him to joint patrol duty inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 殷出入部從不下數百人，又以儀形魁偉，觀者無不聳然。

translations.literal: Yin's retinue when going out numbered no fewer than several hundred; moreover his imposing stature made all who saw him stand in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad his escort numbered at least several hundred men, and his towering frame made every onlooker stand in awe.

sentences.zh: 一日，遽入奏曰：「郊禮在近，兵民大集，臣城外防警，請量給甲仗，以備非常。

translations.literal: One day he suddenly entered and memorialized, saying: "The suburban rites are near, soldiers and civilians are greatly assembled; I guard against alarm outside the city walls—I request a measured allotment of armor and weapons to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: One day he rushed in and memorialized: "The suburban rites are near and troops and civilians are massing. I am responsible for security outside the walls. I ask for a measured issue of arms and armor against emergencies."

sentences.zh: 」太祖難之。

translations.literal: " Taizu found this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was reluctant to grant it.

sentences.zh: 時中外以太祖嬰疾，步履稍難，多不視朝，俯逼郊禋，殷有震主之勢，頗憂之。

translations.literal: At the time, inside and outside court, because Taizu suffered chronic illness, his gait was slightly difficult, and he often did not hold court; with the suburban sacrifice pressing close, Yin had an aura that shook the ruler—many were worried.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court people knew Taizu was chronically ill, walked with difficulty, and often skipped audience. With the sacrifice imminent, Yin's bearing seemed to overshadow the throne, and many were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃力疾坐於滋德殿，殷入起居，即命執之，尋降制流竄，及出都城，遽殺之，眾情乃安。

translations.literal: Taizu then, forcing himself despite illness, sat in Zide Hall; when Yin entered to pay respects, he immediately ordered him seized; soon an edict banished him in exile, and once outside the capital city he was swiftly killed—public sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu forced himself up and sat in Zide Hall. When Yin came to pay his respects he was seized at once. An edict soon banished him, and once he was beyond the capital he was killed without delay. Public anxiety then subsided.

sentences.zh: 是歲春末，鄴城寺鐘懸絕而落，又火光出幡竿之上。

translations.literal: That spring's end, a temple bell in Ye city had its suspension rope break and it fell; fire-light also appeared atop a banner pole.
translations.idiomatic: Late that spring a temple bell in Ye had its rope snap and fell, and fire was seen atop a banner pole.

sentences.zh: 殷之入覲也，都人餞於離亭，上馬失鐙，翻墮於地，人訝其不祥，果及於禍。

translations.literal: When Yin came for audience, the capital people saw him off at the parting pavilion; mounting his horse he lost a stirrup and tumbled to the ground—people marveled at the ill omen, and indeed calamity followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin came to court the people of the capital saw him off at the farewell pavilion. He lost a stirrup mounting his horse and fell to the ground. Onlookers took it for an ill omen—and disaster did follow.

sentences.zh: 太祖尋令澶帥鄭仁誨赴鄴，殷次子為衙內指揮使，不出候謁，仁誨誅之，遷其家屬於登州。

translations.literal: Taizu soon ordered Cangzhou commander Zheng Renhui to go to Ye; Yin's second son was intramural guard commander and did not come out to greet him—Renhui executed him and relocated the family to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu soon sent Cangzhou commander Zheng Renhui to Ye. Yin's second son, intramural guard commander, failed to come out to receive him; Renhui executed him and moved the family to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 何福進，字善長，太原人。

translations.literal: He Fujin, styled Shanchang, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin, styled Shanchang, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父神劍，累贈左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shenjian was posthumously promoted several times to Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenjian was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 福進少從軍，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Fujin entered the army young and was renowned for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: Fujin entered the army in youth and was known for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，郭從謙以兵圍莊宗於大內，福進時為宿衛軍校，獨出死力拒戰於內，後明宗知而嘉之，擢為捧聖軍校，出為磁州刺史，充北面行營先鋒都校。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang reign, Guo Congqian surrounded Emperor Zhuangzong in the inner palace with troops; Fujin was then a guard-army officer on night duty and alone exerted deadly force resisting battle within; later Emperor Mingzong learned and commended him, promoted him to officer of the Pingsheng Army, sent him out as prefect of Ci Prefecture, and made him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tongguang, Guo Congqian besieged Emperor Zhuangzong in the inner palace. Fujin was then a palace guard officer and alone fought to the death inside. Emperor Mingzong learned of it and praised him, promoting him to the Pingsheng guard, then sending him out as prefect of Ci and vanguard commander of the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，自彰聖都虞候率本軍從範延光平鄴，以功歷鄭、隴二州防禦使。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, from adjutant of the Zhangsheng Army he led his own army following Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye; for his merit he successively served as defense commissioner of Zheng and Long prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai, as adjutant of the Zhangsheng army he led his troops with Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye and, for his merit, served in turn as defense commissioner of Zheng and Long prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開運中，由潁州團練使入拜左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun, from regimental commissioner of Ying Prefecture he entered court as Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun he left his post as regimental commissioner of Yingzhou and entered court as Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹陷中原，令中朝文武臣僚凡數十人隨帳北歸，時福進預其行。

translations.literal: When the Khitan seized the Central Plains, they ordered several tens of civil and military officials of the central court to follow the encampment north; at the time Fujin was among those on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan overran the Central Plains they took several dozen central-court officials north with the royal camp, and Fujin was among them.

sentences.zh: 行次鎮州，聞北主已斃，其黨尚據鎮陽，遂與李筠、白再榮之儔合謀力戰，盡逐契丹，據有鎮陽。

translations.literal: Stopping at Zhen Prefecture, they heard the northern ruler had already died but his faction still held Zhenyang; thereupon with Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and their kind they joined in plotting and fought with all their strength, completely driving out the Khitan and seizing Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzhou they heard the Khitan ruler was dead but his followers still held the city. Fujin joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and others in a fierce fight that drove the Khitan out and secured Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖已建號於河東，詔以福進為北面行營馬步都虞候，尋拜曹州防禦使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the time the Han founder had already established his title in Hedong; an edict appointed Fujin adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign headquarters; soon he was appointed defense commissioner of Cao Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder had already proclaimed his reign in Hedong and appointed Fujin adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign, then soon made him defense commissioner of Cao Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 太祖出鎮於鄴，將謀北伐，奏以福進自隨。

translations.literal: Taizu went out to command at Ye and was about to plan a northern campaign; he memorialized that Fujin accompany him personally.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took command at Ye and prepared a northern campaign, he asked that Fujin accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖入平內難，以輔佐功拜忠武軍節度使，不數月，移領鎮州。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered and pacified the inner turmoil, for his supporting merit he was appointed military governor of the Zhongwu Army; within not many months he was transferred to command Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu quelled the court crisis, Fujin was made military governor of the Zhongwu army for his support; within months he was transferred to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，北鄙無事。

translations.literal: Within several years, the northern frontier was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the northern frontier was quiet.

sentences.zh: 及聞太祖將有事於南郊，拜章入覲，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When he heard Taizu was about to conduct affairs at the southern suburb, he memorialized requesting audience, was changed to military governor of the Tianping Army, and given the added title of Co-Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Taizu would perform the southern suburban sacrifice, he memorialized for audience, was transferred to military governor of the Tianping army, and given the added title of Co-Governor.

sentences.zh: 未及之任，卒於東京之私第，年六十有六，時顯德元年正月也。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, he died at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six; it was the first month of the first year of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post he died at his home in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six, in the first month of Xiande 1.

sentences.zh: 累贈中書令。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted several times to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子繼筠，仕皇朝，領建武軍節度使卒。

translations.literal: His son Jijun served the imperial court and died while holding the post of military governor of the Jianwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jijun served the dynasty and died while military governor of the Jianwu army.

sentences.zh: 劉詞，字好謙，元城人。

translations.literal: Liu Ci, styled Haoqian, was a man of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci, styled Haoqian, was a native of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，事故鄴帥楊師厚，以勇悍聞。

translations.literal: During Liang's Zhenming reign, he formerly served Ye commander Yang Shihou and was renowned for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Zhenming era he had served Ye commander Yang Shihou and was known for fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，亦列於麾下，兩河之戰，無不預焉。

translations.literal: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, he too was listed under his banner; in battles of the Two He, there was none in which he did not take part.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Ci joined his ranks and took part in every major battle between the Yellow and the Bian.

sentences.zh: 同光初，為效節軍使，轉劍直指揮使，尋以忤於權臣，出為汝州小校，凡留滯十餘年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was envoy of the Xiaojie Army, transferred to commander of the Jianzhi Army; soon for offending a powerful minister he was sent out as a petty officer of Ru Prefecture, and in all was detained more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was commander of the Xiaojie army, then of the Jianzhi guard. Soon he offended a powerful minister and was demoted to a petty officer at Ru Prefecture, where he languished for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，詔諸道選驍果以實禁衛，由是得入典禁軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, an edict ordered each circuit to select fierce warriors to fill the palace guard; thereby he was able to enter and command the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai an edict ordered each circuit to send its best fighters to fill the palace guard, and through this Ci re-entered guard service.

sentences.zh: 晉初，從侯益收汜水關，佐楊光遠平鄴都，累遷奉國第一軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, he followed Hou Yi to recover the Sishui Pass, assisted Yang Guangyuan in pacifying the Ye capital, and was repeatedly promoted to adjutant of the First Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin he helped Hou Yi recover Sishui Pass and assisted Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Ye, rising to adjutant of the First Fengguo army.

sentences.zh: 後從馬全節伐安陸，敗淮賊萬餘眾，晉祖嘉之，授奉國都校，累加檢校司空。

translations.literal: Later he followed Ma Quanjie to attack Anlu, defeated more than ten thousand Huai bandits; Emperor Zu of Jin commended him, appointed him colonel of the Fengguo Army, and repeatedly added Honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Ma Quanjie against Anlu and routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels. Emperor Zu of Jin praised him, made him colonel of the Fengguo army, and repeatedly promoted him to Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 又從杜重威敗安重榮於宗城。

translations.literal: He also followed Du Chongwei in defeating An Chongrong at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Du Chongwei in defeating An Chongrong at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 及圍鎮陽，詞自登雲梯，身先士伍，以功加檢校司徒、沁州刺史。

translations.literal: When besieging Zhenyang, Ci himself climbed the cloud ladder, took the lead before the ranks of soldiers, and for his merit was given the added titles of Honorary Minister of Education and prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Zhenyang he climbed the assault ladder himself and led the men from the front. For this he was made Honorary Minister of Education and prefect of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時王師方討襄陽，尋命詞兼行營都虞候，襄陽平，遷本州團練使。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial army was campaigning against Xiangyang; soon Ci was ordered to serve concurrently as campaign adjutant; when Xiangyang was pacified, he was transferred to regimental commissioner of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While the court army was campaigning against Xiangyang he was made campaign adjutant. When Xiangyang fell he was made regimental commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在郡歲餘，臨事之暇，必被甲枕戈而臥，人或問之，詞曰：「我以勇敢而登貴仕，不可一日而忘本也。

translations.literal: In the prefecture for more than a year, in leisure from official business he would always don armor, rest his head on his weapon, and lie down; when people asked him, Ci said: "I rose to noble office through courage—I cannot for a single day forget my roots.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a year in the prefecture, whenever he had a spare moment he slept in armor with his weapon for a pillow. When asked why, Ci said: "I won high office through courage. I must not forget that for a single day.

sentences.zh: 若信其溫飽，則筋力有怠，將來何以報國也！

translations.literal: If I trust in warmth and full belly, then sinew and strength will slacken—how in the future shall I repay the state!"
translations.idiomatic: If I grow soft in comfort my strength will fail—how then could I repay the state!"

sentences.zh: 」及漢有天下，復為奉國右廂都校，遙領閬州防禦使。

translations.literal: " When Han possessed all under Heaven, he again became colonel of the Right Wing of the Fengguo Army and held from afar the post of defense commissioner of Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han ruled the realm he again became colonel of the Fengguo army's right wing and held the defense commissionership of Lang Prefecture in absentia.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平鄴，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Following Taizu in pacifying Ye, he was given the added title of Honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu in pacifying Ye and was made Honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，李守貞叛於河中，太祖征之，朝廷以為侍衛步軍都指揮使，遙領寧江軍節度使，充行營馬步都虞候，命分屯於河西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; Taizu campaigned against him; the court appointed Ci commander of the Palace Guard Infantry, military governor of the Ningjiang Army from afar, and campaign adjutant of horse and foot, ordering him to station separately on the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong. Taizu marched against him and the court made Ci commander of the palace guard infantry, military governor of the Ningjiang army in absentia, and campaign adjutant of horse and foot, with orders to encamp west of the river.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，守貞遣敢死之士數千，夜入其營。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Shouzhen sent several thousand death-defying warriors who entered his camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Shouzhen sent several thousand suicide troops to raid his camp by night.

sentences.zh: 皆怖懼不知所為，惟詞神氣自若，令於軍中曰：「此小盜耳，不足驚也。

translations.literal: All were terrified and did not know what to do; only Ci's spirit and bearing were as usual; he ordered within the army, saying: "These are petty bandits—nothing to be alarmed about.
translations.idiomatic: The men panicked, but Ci remained calm and told the army: "These are only petty raiders—nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」遂免胄橫戈，叱短兵以擊之，賊眾大敗而退。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he removed his helmet, laid his weapon across him, shouted at short weapons to strike them, and the bandit host was greatly defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He doffed his helmet, seized a spear, and led the close fighters in a charge. The enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 自是守貞喪膽，不復有奔突之意。

translations.literal: From this Shouzhen lost his gall and no longer had the will to make sudden raids.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shouzhen lost heart and made no more daring sorties.

sentences.zh: 河中平，太祖嘉之，表其功為華州節度使，歲餘，移鎮邢臺。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Taizu commended him and memorialized his merit as military governor of Huazhou; after more than a year he was transferred to command Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhong was pacified Taizu praised him and recommended him as military governor of Huazhou. After a year he was transferred to Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the mandate, Ci was given the added title of Co-Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne Ci was given the added title of Co-Governor.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，改鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year he was transferred to command Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the third year he was transferred to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，世宗親征劉崇，詞奉命領所部兵隨駕，行及高平南，遇樊愛能等自北退回，且言官軍已敗，止詞不行，詞不聽，疾驅而北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, Emperor Shizong personally campaigned against Liu Chong; Ci received orders to lead his own troops following the imperial carriage; when they reached south of Gaoping they met Fan Aineng and others returning from the north and saying the imperial army had been defeated—they stopped Ci from advancing; Ci would not listen and spurred swiftly north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande Emperor Shizong personally marched against Liu Chong. Ci led his troops with the imperial train. South of Gaoping he met Fan Aineng and others retreating from the north, claiming the army had been beaten. They tried to hold Ci back, but he would not listen and galloped north at once.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞而嘉之，尋命為隨駕都部署，又授河東道行營副部署。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard and commended him; soon he was ordered to be overall commander accompanying the carriage, and was also appointed deputy overall commander of the Hedong campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong heard of it and praised him, soon making him overall commander with the imperial train and deputy commander of the Hedong campaign.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，車駕還京，授永興軍節度使，加兼侍中，行京兆尹。

translations.literal: That summer, when the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was appointed military governor of the Yongxing Army, given the concurrent title of Palace Attendant, and acted as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the emperor returned to the capital, Ci was made military governor of the Yongxing army, given the concurrent title of Palace Attendant, and commissioned as acting metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，以疾卒於鎮，年六十有五。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year he died of illness at his command, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the second year he died of illness at his post, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，謚曰忠惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Loyal and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous name Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 詞發身軍校，亟歷戎事，常以忠勇自負。

translations.literal: Ci rose from a guard-army officer, repeatedly passed through military affairs, and always took pride in loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Ci had risen from a guard officer through many campaigns and always prided himself on loyalty and courage.

sentences.zh: 洎領藩鎮，能靖恭為治，無苛政以撓民，謚以忠惠，議者韙之。

translations.literal: When he came to lead a military prefecture, he was able to govern with quiet respect; there were no harsh policies to vex the people; his posthumous title Loyal and Kind—commentators approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed a command he ruled with quiet dignity and imposed no harsh policies on the people. Commentators agreed that the posthumous name Loyal and Kind was apt.

sentences.zh: 子延欽，仕皇朝為控鶴廂使。

translations.literal: His son Yanqin served the imperial court as commissioner of the Konghe Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanqin served the dynasty as commissioner of the Konghe wing.

sentences.zh: 史彥超，雲州人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yanchao was a man of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanchao was a native of Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性驍獷，有膽氣，累功至龍捷都指揮使。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and unruly; he had daring spirit; through accumulated merit he reached commander of the Longjie Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and unruly by nature, he was bold in spirit and rose through merit to commander of the Longjie army.

sentences.zh: 太祖之赴內難，彥超以本軍從。

translations.literal: When Taizu went to resolve the inner turmoil, Yanchao followed with his own army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched to quell the court crisis, Yanchao followed with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 國初，與虎捷都指揮使何徵戍晉州，會劉崇與契丹入寇，攻圍州城月餘，是時本州無帥，知州王萬敢不協物情，彥超與何徵協力固拒，累挫敵鋒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, together with Huzhe army commander He Zheng he garrisoned Jin Prefecture; when Liu Chong and the Khitan invaded, they attacked and besieged the prefectural city for more than a month; at the time the prefecture had no commander; prefect Wang Wang'an did not harmonize with public sentiment; Yanchao and He Zheng joined strength in firm resistance and repeatedly blunted the enemy's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty he and Huzhe commander He Zheng garrisoned Jinzhou. When Liu Chong and the Khitan invaded they besieged the city for more than a month. The prefecture had no military governor, and prefect Wang Wang'an was unpopular. Yanchao and He Zheng held the city together and repeatedly repulsed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 攻擊日急，禦捍有備，軍政甚嚴，居人無擾。

translations.literal: As attacks grew daily more urgent, defense and resistance were prepared; military government was very strict; residents were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: As the assaults intensified their defenses held firm, military discipline was strict, and the townspeople were left unharmed.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷遣樞密使王峻總兵為援，敵兵宵遁。

translations.literal: When the court sent Grand Councilor Wang Jun to command troops as relief, the enemy army fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent Grand Councilor Wang Jun with relief troops, the enemy fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其善守之功，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Taizu commended their merit in good defense and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised their successful defense and rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授龍捷右廂都指揮使，尋授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed commander of the Right Wing of the Longjie Army; soon he was appointed defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of the Longjie army's right wing, then defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉崇之寇潞州也，車駕親征，以彥超為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong raided Luzhou, the imperial carriage personally campaigned and made Yanchao vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong attacked Luzhou the emperor marched in person and made Yanchao vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 高平之戰，先登陷陣，以功授華州節度使，先鋒如故。

translations.literal: At the battle of Gaoping he was first to ascend and break the formation; for his merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou, vanguard as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoping he was first over the wall and into the enemy line. For this he was made military governor of Huazhou while keeping his vanguard command.

sentences.zh: 大軍至河東城下，契丹營於忻、代之間，遙應賊勢，詔天雄軍節度使符彥卿率諸將屯忻州以拒之。

translations.literal: When the great army reached below the Hedong city wall, the Khitan encamped between Xin and Dai, responding to the bandit power from afar; an edict ordered Tianxiong military governor Fu Yanqing to lead the generals to station at Xin Prefecture to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army reached Hedong the Khitan camped between Xin and Dai in support of the enemy. Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was ordered to hold Xinzhou with the other generals and block them.

sentences.zh: 彥卿襲契丹於忻口。

translations.literal: Yanqing raided the Khitan at Xinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing attacked the Khitan at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 彥超以先鋒軍追蕃寇，離大軍稍遠，賊兵伏發，為賊所陷。

translations.literal: Yanchao with the vanguard army pursued the barbarian bandits; separating slightly from the great army, enemy troops sprang an ambush and he was trapped by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao pursued the enemy with the vanguard, straying somewhat from the main force. Ambushers struck and he was cut off.

sentences.zh: 世宗痛惜久之，詔贈太師，示加等也，仍命優恤其家焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong grieved long; an edict posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor, showing added rank, and still ordered generous care for his family.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him deeply. An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor—an exceptional honor—and ordered special care for his family.

sentences.zh: 史懿，字繼美，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yi, styled Jimei, was a man of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi, styled Jimei, was a native of Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名犯太祖廟諱，故改焉。

translations.literal: His original personal name violated the taboo of Taizu's temple name, and therefore it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name violated the taboo on Taizu's temple name, so it was changed.

sentences.zh: 父建瑭，事唐莊宗為先鋒都校，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Jiantang served Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong as vanguard colonel; the Book of Tang has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiantang had served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang as vanguard colonel and has a biography in the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗之伐鎮陽，時建瑭為流矢所中而卒，懿時年甫弱冠，莊宗以其父歿於王事，召拜昭德軍使，俄遷先鋒左右廂都校，俾嗣其家聲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhenyang, at the time Jiantang was struck by a stray arrow and died; Yi was then just past weak cap; Emperor Zhuangzong because his father died in royal service summoned and appointed him envoy of the Zhaode Army, soon transferred to colonel of the Left and Right Wings of the vanguard, causing him to inherit his family's renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong attacked Zhenyang, Jiantang was killed by a stray arrow. Yi was then barely twenty. Zhuangzong, honoring his father's death in imperial service, appointed Yi envoy of the Zhaode army and soon colonel of the vanguard's left and right wings so that he might carry on the family name.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為涿州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, he served as prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉初，由趙州刺史遷洺州團練使，尋歷亳、鳳二州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, from Zhao Prefecture prefect he was transferred to regimental training commissioner of Luozhou; soon he successively served as defense commissioner of Bo and Feng Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty he moved from prefect of Zhao to regimental training commissioner of Luozhou, then served in turn as defense commissioner of Bo and Feng Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 晉祖以其弟翰尚晉國長公主，故尤所註意。

translations.literal: The Jin ancestor because his younger brother Han married the eldest princess of Jin State therefore paid him especially close attention.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder favored him all the more because his younger brother Han had married the eldest princess of Jin.

sentences.zh: 天福中，授彰武軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era, he was appointed military governor and observation envoy in waiting of the Zhangwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era he was made military governor and observation envoy in waiting of the Zhangwu army.

sentences.zh: 開運初，歷澶、貝二鎮節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, he successively served as military governor of the two garrison districts of Chan and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyun era he served in turn as military governor of the Chan and Bei garrisons.

sentences.zh: 三年，移鎮涇原。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to command at Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，契丹入中原，時四方征鎮為契丹所召者靡不灊至，惟懿堅壁拒命，仍送款於漢祖。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan entered the Central Plains; at the time of the military garrisons throughout the realm summoned by the Khitan, none failed to arrive in throngs; only Yi fortified his walls and refused orders, yet still sent submission to the Han ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan swept into the Central Plains. Every garrison the Khitan summoned sent troops at once—only Yi held his walls and refused, while secretly pledging loyalty to the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，就拜檢校太尉、同平章事，及賜功臣名號。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, he was at once appointed acting Grand Commandant and Co-Governor, and granted an honorific title of meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Han dynasty held the realm, he was immediately made acting Grand Commandant and Co-Governor and given a meritorious minister's honorific title.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加檢校太師、兼侍中，進封邠國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was given added acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent palace attendant, and advanced to Duke of Bin State.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he was further made acting Grand Preceptor and palace attendant and promoted to Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年春，以抱病歸朝。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiande, he returned to court bearing illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xiande 1 he returned to court, ill.

translations.literal: (Annotation:
translations.idiomatic: (From the Eastern Capital Brief Account:

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》：周太祖常諭廷璋圖涇帥史懿，廷璋屏左右，示以詔書，懿受代入朝，遂免禍。）〉

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Brief Account, Biography of Yang Tingzhang: Zhou Taizu often instructed Tingzhang to scheme against Shi Yi, military governor of Jing; Tingzhang dismissed those around him and showed him the edict; Yi accepted replacement and entered court, thus escaping disaster.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Brief Account, Biography of Yang Tingzhang: Zhou Taizu often urged Tingzhang to move against Shi Yi, governor of Jing Prefecture. Tingzhang sent away his attendants and showed him the imperial order. Yi accepted relief from command and came to court, thereby avoiding ruin.)〉

sentences.zh: 途經洛，卒於其第，年六十三。

translations.literal: Passing through Luo, he died at his residence, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: En route through Luoyang he died at his home, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Chief Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Chief Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王令溫，字順之，瀛州河間人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lingwen, styled Shunzhi, was a man of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingwen, styled Shunzhi, was a native of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父迪，德州刺史，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Di was prefect of De Prefecture and was posthumously advanced repeatedly to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Di had been prefect of De Prefecture and was posthumously raised to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 令溫少以武勇稱，初隸唐莊宗麾下，稍遷廳直軍校。

translations.literal: Lingwen in youth was famed for martial courage; initially he served under Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and was gradually promoted to hall-direct colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen was known from youth for martial valor. He first served under Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang and rose gradually to hall-direct colonel.

sentences.zh: 明宗之為統帥，嘗與契丹戰於上谷，明宗臨陣馬逸，為敵所迫，令溫乃以所乘馬授明宗，而自力戰，飛矢連發，敵兵為之稍卻。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was supreme commander, he once fought the Khitan at Shanggu; Mingzong at the battle line had his horse bolt and was pressed by the enemy; Lingwen then gave the horse he was riding to Mingzong and fought on his own strength, loosing arrows in rapid succession, and the enemy troops for this reason retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: While Mingzong was still supreme commander he fought the Khitan at Shanggu. Mingzong's horse bolted in the fighting and the enemy closed in. Lingwen gave Mingzong his own mount and fought on foot, loosing arrow after arrow until the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位，歷遷神武彰聖都校。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Shenwu and Zhangsheng armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong took the throne, Lingwen rose to command the Shenwu and Zhangsheng armies.

sentences.zh: 晉初，自淄州刺史遷洺州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, from Zi Prefecture prefect he was transferred to regimental training commissioner of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty he moved from prefect of Zi to regimental training commissioner of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 及安重榮稱兵於鎮州，晉祖以令溫為行營馬軍都指揮使，與都帥杜重威敗賊於宗城，以功授亳州防禦使，尋拜永清軍節度使。

translations.literal: When An Chongrong raised troops at Zhen Prefecture, the Jin ancestor made Lingwen campaign horse-army commander; together with supreme commander Du Chongwei he defeated the rebels at Zongcheng, and for his merit was appointed defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture; soon he was appointed military governor of the Yongqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou the Jin founder made Lingwen campaign commander of the horse army. With Du Chongwei he routed the rebels at Zongcheng. For this he was made defense commissioner of Bozhou and soon military governor of the Yongqing army.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹來寇，時令溫奉詔入朝，契丹遂陷貝州，其家屬因沒於契丹。

translations.literal: Just then the Khitan came to raid; at the time Lingwen was obeying an edict to enter court, and the Khitan then captured Bei Prefecture; his family members thereby fell into Khitan hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, Lingwen had been called to court by imperial order. The Khitan took Beizhou and his family was carried off.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝憫之，授武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Jin Young Emperor took pity on him and appointed him military governor of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor of Jin took pity on him and made him military governor of the Wusheng army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮延州，又遷靈武。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to command at Yan Prefecture, and again moved to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Yanzhou, then to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，復為永清軍節度使，尋改安州。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, he again became military governor of the Yongqing Army; soon he was changed to An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Han dynasty held the realm he again commanded the Yongqing army, then was reassigned to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 國初，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, he was given added acting Grand Commandant and Co-Governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was further made acting Grand Commandant and Co-Governor.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，遷鎮安軍節度使，罷鎮歸闕。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to military governor of the Zhen'an Army, dismissed from his command and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded he was made military governor of the Zhen'an army, then relieved of command and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年夏，以疾卒，時年六十有二，詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Xiande, he died of illness; at the time he was sixty-two; an edict posthumously granted him palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xiande 3 he died of illness at sixty-two. An edict posthumously made him palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 長子銳，仕皇朝為內職。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rui served the imperial court as an inner-service official.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rui held an inner-court post under the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 次子廣，歷諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His second son Guang successively served as great general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Guang rose through the ranks to great general of the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 李懷忠，字光孝，太原晉陽人。

translations.literal: Li Huaizong, styled Guangxiao, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizong, styled Guangxiao, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父海，本府軍校。

translations.literal: His father Hai was a military colonel of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hai had been a military colonel of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷忠形質魁壯，初事唐莊宗，隸於保衛軍。

translations.literal: Huaizong's physique was tall and strong; he initially served Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and was enrolled in the guard army.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizong was tall and powerfully built. He first served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang in the guard army.

sentences.zh: 夾城之役，懷忠率先登城，以功補本軍副兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the battle of Jiacheng, Huaizong was first to ascend the wall; for his merit he was appointed deputy horse commander of his army.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Jiacheng Huaizong was first over the wall. For this he was made deputy horse commander of his unit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定山東，累遷保衛軍使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, he was repeatedly promoted to commissioner of the guard army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, Huaizong rose repeatedly until he commanded the guard army.

sentences.zh: 天成中，歷陜府、許州、滄州都指揮使，遙領辰州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, he successively served as commander of Shan Prefecture, Xuzhou, and Cangzhou, and remotely held the post of Chen Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he served in turn as commander of Shan Prefecture, Xuzhou, and Cangzhou while holding the nominal post of Chenzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，以河西蕃部寇鈔，命懷忠屯方渠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, because western-river barbarian tribes raided and plundered, he was ordered to station Huaizong at Fangqu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai, with western tribes raiding the Hexi frontier, Huaizong was ordered to garrison Fangqu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖受命，以懷忠故人，召典禁兵，三遷護聖左右廂都指揮使，遙領壽州節度使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When the Jin ancestor received the mandate, because Huaizong was an old acquaintance he summoned him to command the forbidden troops; after three promotions he became commander of the left and right wings of the Husheng guard, remotely held military governor of Shou Prefecture, and acting Senior Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder took power he summoned Huaizong, an old comrade, to command the palace guard. Three promotions later he commanded the left and right wings of the Husheng guard, held the nominal post of Shouzhou military governor, and was acting Senior Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為同州節度使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he became military governor of Tong Prefecture and acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military governor of Tongzhou and acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，入為右羽林統軍，改左武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he entered court as commander of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and was changed to senior general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded he entered court as commander of the right imperial guard and was then made senior general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，以太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: During Guangshun, he retired as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangshun era he retired with the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年夏卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year he died, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the third year, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 白文珂，字德溫，太原人也。

translations.literal: Bai Wenke, styled Dewen, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenke, styled Dewen, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖辯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Bian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather's name was Bian.

sentences.zh: 父君成，遼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Juncheng was prefect of Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juncheng had been prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 文珂初事後唐武皇，補河東牙將，改遼州副使。

translations.literal: Wenke initially served Later Tang's Martial Emperor, was appointed a Hedong yamen general, and was changed to vice commissioner of Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke first served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang as a Hedong yamen general, then became vice commissioner of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，轉振武都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to commander of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded he was made commander of the Zhenwu army.

sentences.zh: 天成中，鎮州節度使王建立表為本州馬步軍都指揮使，遙授舒州刺史、檢校司空，歷青州、魏府都指揮使，歷瀛、蔚、忻、代四州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, Zhen Prefecture military governor Wang Jianli memorialized recommending him as horse-and-foot commander of that prefecture; he was remotely appointed prefect of Shu Prefecture and acting Minister of Works; he successively served as commander of Qing Prefecture and Wei Prefecture; he successively served as prefect of Ying, Yu, Xin, and Dai Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era Wang Jianli, military governor of Zhenzhou, recommended him as horse-and-foot commander of the prefecture. He received the nominal posts of Shu prefect and acting Minister of Works, then commanded at Qingzhou and Weizhou and served in turn as prefect of Ying, Yu, Xin, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 領代州日，兼蕃漢馬步都部署。

translations.literal: On the days when he held Daizhou, he concurrently served as overall deployer of barbarian and Han horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: While holding Daizhou he also commanded the combined Han and tribal horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖鎮並門，表為副留守、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu held Bingmen, he memorialized recommending him as deputy regent and acting Senior Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu held Bingzhou he recommended Wenke as deputy regent and acting Senior Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 漢國初建，授河中節度使、西南面招討使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When the Han state was newly established, he was appointed military governor of Hezhong, southwest pacification commissioner, and acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Han dynasty he was made military governor of Hezhong, southwest pacification commissioner, and acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 漢祖定兩京，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Han ancestor settled the two capitals, he was changed to military governor of the Tianping Army and given added Co-Governor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han founder secured the two capitals, Wenke was made military governor of the Tianping army and given the added title of Co-Governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮陜州，檢校太師。

translations.literal: Before long he was stationed at Shan Prefecture as acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted to Shanzhou as acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 會河中李守貞叛，詔充河中府行營都部署。

translations.literal: Just then Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong; an edict appointed him overall campaign deployer for Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong an edict made Wenke overall campaign commander for the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時文珂已老，朝議恐非守貞之敵，乃命太祖西征。

translations.literal: At the time Wenke was already old; court deliberation feared he was no match for Shouzhen, and therefore ordered Taizu to campaign west.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke was by then old, and the court feared he could not stand against Shouzhen, so Taizu was ordered west.

sentences.zh: 河中平，文珂授西京留守、河南尹。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Wenke was appointed regent of the western capital and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hezhong was pacified, Wenke was made regent of the western capital and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，加兼中書令，頃之，以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, he was given added concurrent Chief Councilor of the Central Secretariat; before long he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne Wenke was further made Chief Councilor of the Central Secretariat; soon afterward he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，封晉國公。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin State.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，卒於西京，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande, he died at the western capital, age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 1 he died at the western capital, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: Court audience was suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspended audience for one day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 子廷誨，仕皇朝，歷諸衛將軍卒。

translations.literal: His son Tinghui served the imperial court, successively served as guard general, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tinghui served the dynasty, rose through the guard ranks, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 白延遇，字希望，太原人也。

translations.literal: Bai Yanyu, styled Xiwang, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanyu, styled Xiwang, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼畜於晉之公宮，年十三，從晉祖伐蜀，以趫悍見稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was raised in the Jin ducal palace; at age thirteen he followed the Jin ancestor in campaigning against Shu and was famed for swift fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised from childhood in the Jin ducal household. At thirteen he followed the Jin founder against Shu and won renown for his swift, fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 晉有天下，歷典禁軍，累遷至檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Jin possessed the realm, he successively commanded the forbidden army and was repeatedly promoted until acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin held the realm he served in the palace guard and rose to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天福中，晉祖在鄴，安重榮叛於鎮州，帥眾數萬詣闕而來，晉祖命杜重威統諸將以禦之。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era, the Jin ancestor was at Ye; An Chongrong rebelled at Zhen Prefecture and led a host of tens of thousands toward the capital; the Jin ancestor ordered Du Chongwei to command the generals to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era, with the Jin founder at Ye, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and marched tens of thousands of men on the capital. The Jin founder ordered Du Chongwei to lead the generals against him.

sentences.zh: 時延遇不預其行，乃泣告晉祖，願以身先，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Yanyu was not included in the campaign; he then wept and told the Jin ancestor that he wished to take the lead in person, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu had not been chosen for the campaign. He wept before the Jin founder and begged to lead the van; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及陣於宗城，延遇率其屬先犯之，斬級數十，戰既酣，而劍亦折，諸將由是推伏。

translations.literal: When the armies formed at Zongcheng, Yanyu led his followers first to strike them, beheading several tens of heads; once the battle had grown fierce his sword also broke; the generals thereby submitted in respect.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle line at Zongcheng Yanyu led his men in the first assault and took dozens of heads. In the heat of battle his sword snapped, and the other generals were won over by his courage.

sentences.zh: 晉祖聞之，即命中使以寶劍良馬賜之。

translations.literal: When the Jin ancestor heard of this, he immediately ordered a palace envoy to bestow on him a treasured sword and fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder heard of it and at once sent a palace envoy with a treasured sword and fine horse.

sentences.zh: 常山平，以功授檢校司徒，充馬軍左廂都校。

translations.literal: When Changshan was pacified, for his merit he was appointed acting Minister over the Masses and made colonel of the left wing of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshan was pacified he was made acting Minister over the Masses and colonel of the horse army's left wing.

sentences.zh: 後出為汾州刺史，遷復州防禦使。

translations.literal: Later he went out as prefect of Fen Prefecture and was transferred to defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became prefect of Fenzhou, then defense commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 國初，加檢校太保，尋受代歸闕。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, he was given added acting Senior Grand Mentor; soon he was replaced and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was further made acting Senior Grand Mentor, then relieved and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 屬太祖親征兗海，以延遇為先鋒都校，兗州平，授齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Just then Taizu personally campaigned against Yan and Hai; he made Yanyu vanguard colonel; when Yan Prefecture was pacified, he was appointed defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched in person against Yan and Hai he made Yanyu vanguard colonel. After Yanzhou fell Yanyu was made defense commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改兗州防禦使。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year, he was changed to defense commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was reassigned as defense commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 在兗二年，為政有聞，人甚安之，州民數百詣闕，乞立德政碑以頌其美。

translations.literal: During two years at Yan, his governance was noted; the people were greatly at ease; several hundred citizens of the prefecture went to court requesting that a stele of virtuous administration be erected to praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In two years at Yanzhou his rule won wide praise and the people lived in peace. Hundreds of local citizens went to court asking that a stele be raised to honor his good governance.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年冬，世宗命宰臣李穀為淮南道軍都部署，乃詔延遇為先鋒都校。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Xiande, Shizong appointed chief minister Li Gu overall campaign deployer of the Huainan circuit army, and then issued an edict making Yanyu vanguard colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Xiande 2 Shizong made chief minister Li Gu overall commander of the Huainan campaign and ordered Yanyu to serve as vanguard colonel.

sentences.zh: 三年春，帥其所部與韓令坤先入揚州，軍聲甚振，尋命以別部屯於盛唐，前後敗淮賊萬餘眾。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, he led his command together with Han Lingkun first into Yang Prefecture; the army's reputation was greatly shaken; soon he was ordered with a separate division to station at Sheng Tang; before and after he defeated Huai rebels numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he and Han Lingkun led their troops into Yangzhou first, and the army's fame spread far. Soon he was ordered to hold Sheng Tang with a separate detachment and in repeated engagements routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，世宗回自壽春，制以延遇為同州節度使，未赴任，復命帥眾南征。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year, Shizong returned from Shouchun; by decree Yanyu was made military governor of Tong Prefecture; before he took up the post he was again ordered to lead troops on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year Shizong returned from Shouchun and appointed Yanyu military governor of Tongzhou. Before he could take up the post he was ordered south again at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以疾卒於濠州城下。

translations.literal: That winter, he died of illness below the walls of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he died of illness beneath the walls of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。

translations.literal: Tang Jinsi was a man of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jinsi was a native of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼以屠狗為業，善角觝戲。

translations.literal: In youth he made dog butchery his trade and was skilled at wrestling entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he butchered dogs for a living and excelled at wrestling shows.

sentences.zh: 初事偽蜀為軍校。

translations.literal: Initially he served False Shu as a military colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the puppet Shu state as a military colonel.

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，莊宗命魏王繼岌帥師伐蜀，時景思以所部戍於固鎮，首以其城降於繼岌，乃授興州刺史，為貝州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: During Tang's Tongguang era, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Prince Jiji of Wei to lead an army against Shu; at the time Jinsi with his command garrisoned Guzhen and was first to surrender that city to Jiji; he was then appointed prefect of Xing Prefecture and made campaign staff officer of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang era Zhuangzong ordered Prince Jiji of Wei to lead an army against Shu. Jinsi was then garrisoning Guzhen with his unit and was the first to surrender the town to Jiji. He was made prefect of Xingzhou and campaign staff officer of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹攻其城，因陷於幕庭，趙延壽素知其名，令隸於帳下，署為所部壕寨使。

translations.literal: Just then the Khitan attacked his city and he thereby fell into their camp court; Zhao Yanshou had long known his name and had him serve under his banner, appointing him trench-camp commissioner of his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked his city he fell into their hands. Zhao Yanshou, who had long known his reputation, took him into his service and made him trench-camp commissioner under his command.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹據中原，以景思為亳州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan held the Central Plains and made Jinsi defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyun era, with the Khitan holding the Central Plains, Jinsi was made defense commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 領事之日，會草寇數萬攻圍其城，景思悉力以拒之。

translations.literal: On the days when he took office, it happened that grass-bandit forces numbering tens of thousands attacked and besieged his city; Jinsi exhausted his strength to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he took office, bandit armies numbering in the tens of thousands besieged the city. Jinsi threw all his strength into the defense.

sentences.zh: 後數日城陷，景思挺身而出，使人告於鄰郡，得援軍數百，逐其草寇，復有其城，亳民賴是以濟。

translations.literal: Several days later the city fell; Jinsi stepped forward boldly, sent men to report to neighboring prefectures, obtained relief troops numbering in the hundreds, drove away the grass bandits, recovered his city, and the people of Bo thereby were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the city fell. Jinsi broke out boldly, sent word to neighboring prefectures, and brought back several hundred relief troops. He drove off the bandits, retook the city, and the people of Bozhou were saved.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改授鄧州行軍司馬，常郁郁不得志，後受代歸闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, he was changed and appointed campaign staff officer of Deng Prefecture; he was often depressed and without achieving his ambitions; later he was replaced and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty he was reassigned as campaign staff officer of Dengzhou. He remained frustrated and unfulfilled until he was relieved and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，命景思為沿淮巡檢使，屢挫淮賊。

translations.literal: During Qianyou, he was appointed Jinsi inspector along the Huai River, and repeatedly defeated Huai rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianyou era Jinsi was made inspector along the Huai River and repeatedly routed Huai rebels.

sentences.zh: 時史宏肇淫刑黷貨，多織羅南北富商殺之，奪其財，大開告密之門。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongyin used excessive punishments and corrupt goods; he often fabricated charges against north-and-south merchants and killed them, seized their wealth, and widely opened the gate of secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shi Hongyin abused the law for profit, framing merchants from north and south, executing them, and seizing their wealth while encouraging informers at every turn.

sentences.zh: 景思部下有仆夫，希求無厭，雖委曲待之，不滿其心，一日拂衣而去，見宏肇，言景思受淮南厚賂，私貯器械，欲為內應。

translations.literal: Under Jinsi's command there was a servant; his greedy demands were insatiable; though Jinsi treated him with every consideration, he did not satisfy the man's heart; one day he shook out his robes and left, saw Hongyin, and said that Jinsi had received heavy bribes from Huainan, secretly stored weapons, and intended to serve as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jinsi's followers was a servant whose greed knew no limit. Though Jinsi treated him with every courtesy, the man was never satisfied. One day he stormed off, sought out Hongyin, and accused Jinsi of taking heavy bribes from Huainan, hoarding weapons in secret, and plotting to serve as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 宏肇即令親吏殿三十騎往收之，告者謂收吏曰：「景思多力，十夫之敵也，見便殺之，不然則無及矣。

translations.literal: Hongyin immediately ordered his personal clerk to lead thirty riders to arrest him; the accuser told the arresting officers: "Jinsi is very strong, a match for ten men; on sight kill him, otherwise it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyin at once sent his personal clerk with thirty riders to seize Jinsi. The accuser told the arresting officers: "Jinsi is immensely strong—a match for ten men. Kill him on sight, or it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 」收騎至，景思迎接。

translations.literal: " The arresting riders arrived, and Jinsi went out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: " When the arresting riders arrived, Jinsi went out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 有欲擒之者，景思以兩手抱之，大呼曰：「冤哉！

translations.literal: Some wished to seize him; Jinsi with both hands embraced one of them and shouted loudly: "Injustice!
translations.idiomatic: When some moved to seize him, Jinsi threw his arms around one of them and cried out: "This is injustice!

sentences.zh: 景思何罪？

translations.literal: What crime has Jinsi?
translations.idiomatic: What crime has Jinsi committed?

sentences.zh: 設若有罪，死亦非晚，何不容披雪？

translations.literal: Suppose there were a crime—death would not yet be late; why not allow clearing of the snow?
translations.idiomatic: Even if I were guilty, death would not come too late—why will you not let me clear my name?

sentences.zh: 公等皆丈夫，安忍如此！

translations.literal: You gentlemen are all men—how can you bear to be like this!
translations.idiomatic: You are all men—how can you bear to act this way!

sentences.zh: 」都將命釋之，引告者面證景思，言受淮南賂。

translations.literal: " The commander ordered him released, brought the accuser face to face to confront Jinsi, and said he had received Huainan bribes.
translations.idiomatic: " The commander ordered him released and brought the accuser forward to confront Jinsi face to face, charging that he had taken Huainan bribes.

sentences.zh: 景思曰：「我從人家人並在此，若有十緡貯積，亦是受賂。

translations.literal: Jinsi said: "My followers and family members are all here; if there were ten strings of cash stored away, that too would be taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi said: "My followers and my household are all here. If I had even ten strings of cash put by, that would count as taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 言我貯甲仗，除官賜外，有一事亦是私貯。

translations.literal: He said that I hoard armor and weapons; apart from official salaries and gifts, there is one matter that is also private hoarding.
translations.idiomatic: He claims I am hoarding arms and armor. Aside from my official pay and gifts, he says even one other possession would count as secret stores.

sentences.zh: 」使者搜索其家，惟衣一笥，軍籍糧簿而已，乃寬之。

translations.literal: " The envoys searched his home and found only one chest of clothes and military registers and grain ledgers—thereupon they relaxed the case against him.
translations.idiomatic: " The searchers combed his house and found only a single chest of clothes plus muster rolls and ration books, and so they eased their grip on him.

sentences.zh: 景思曰：「使但械系送我入京。

translations.literal: Jinsi said: "Commissioner, simply bind me in fetters and send me to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi said: "Sir, just put me in chains and send me to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」先是，景思別有紀綱王知權者，在京，聞景思被誣，乃見史宏肇曰：「唐景思赤心為國，某服事三十年，孝於父母，義於朋友，被此誣罔，何以伸陳。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Jinsi had a separate steward named Wang Zhiquan in the capital; hearing Jinsi was slandered, he went to see Shi Hongzhao and said: "Tang Jinsi serves the state with a loyal heart; I have served him thirty years—filial to parents, righteous to friends—and now he suffers this false charge; how can I make his case heard?
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Jinsi had a steward named Wang Zhiquan in the capital. When he heard Jinsi had been framed, he went to Shi Hongzhao and said: "Tang Jinsi has given his loyal heart to the state. I have served him thirty years and know him to be filial to his parents and true to his friends. Framed like this, how can his case be heard?

sentences.zh: 某請先下獄，願公追劾景思，免至冤橫。

translations.literal: I beg to enter prison first and ask that Your Excellency pursue and investigate Jinsi, sparing him unjust ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be thrown into prison myself first, and I beg you to investigate Jinsi properly so he is not destroyed by injustice.

sentences.zh: 」宏肇湣之，令在獄，日與酒食。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao pitied him and had him kept in prison, giving him wine and food each day.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao was moved and kept him in custody, sending him wine and food every day.

sentences.zh: 景思既桎梏就路，潁、亳之人隨至京師，眾保證之。

translations.literal: Once Jinsi was shackled on the road, people of Ying and Bo followed him to the capital, and the multitude vouched for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinsi was led away in shackles, people from Ying and Bo followed him all the way to the capital to testify on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 宏肇乃令鞫告事者，具伏誣陷，即斬之，遂奏釋景思。

translations.literal: Hongzhao then ordered the accuser interrogated; he fully confessed to false impeachment and was immediately beheaded; he then memorialized to release Jinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao had the accuser interrogated. He confessed fully to the frame-up and was executed at once. Hongzhao then memorialized for Jinsi's release.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，河東劉崇帥眾來寇，世宗親總六師以禦之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, Liu Chong of Hedong led a host to raid; Emperor Shizong personally commanded the Six Armies to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande Liu Chong of Hedong invaded with a large force, and Emperor Shizong personally took command of the imperial armies to meet him.

sentences.zh: 及陣於高平，景思於世宗馬前距踴數四，且曰：「願賜臣堅甲一聯，以觀臣之效用。

translations.literal: When the armies formed at Gaoping, Jinsi leaped and stamped four times before Shizong's horse and said: "I beg to be granted one suit of stout armor, that Your Majesty may see my usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle line at Gaoping, Jinsi bounded forward four times before Shizong's horse and cried: "Grant me a suit of strong armor so Your Majesty may see what I can do.

sentences.zh: 」世宗由是知其名，因以高平陣所得降軍數千人，署為效順指揮，命景思董之，使於淮上。

translations.literal: " Shizong thereby came to know his name; he thereupon took several thousand surrendered troops gained at the Gaoping battle line, appointed them the Obedient Submission Command, ordered Jinsi to supervise them, and sent him to the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong took notice of him and assigned him several thousand surrendered troops from Gaoping as the Loyal Submission command, with orders to lead them on the Huai front.

sentences.zh: 三年春，世宗親征淮甸，景思繼有戰功，乃命遙領饒州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, Shizong personally campaigned in the Huai region; Jinsi continued to win battle merit, and he was ordered to hold from afar the post of prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year Shizong marched in person on the Huai. Jinsi kept distinguishing himself in battle and was given the prefecture of Raozhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改授濠州行刺史，令帥眾攻圍濠州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred and appointed acting prefect of Hao Prefecture, ordered to lead troops to attack and besiege Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting prefect of Haozhou and ordered to lead troops in the siege of that city.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，因力戰，為賊鋒所傷，數日而卒。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year, fighting with all his strength, he was wounded by the enemy vanguard and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the fourth year he fought at full force, was struck down by the enemy van, and died within days.

sentences.zh: 世宗甚憫之，詔贈武清軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shizong deeply pitied him and by edict posthumously made him military governor of the Wuqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him deeply and posthumously made him military governor of the Wuqing army.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古為人臣者，望重則必危，功崇則難保，自非賢者，疇能免之。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: From antiquity, for those who serve as ministers, when renown is heavy peril is sure to follow, and when merit is lofty it is hard to preserve—unless one is worthy, who can escape this?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From antiquity, ministers whose standing grew weighty were sure to face peril, and those whose merit towered high were hard to preserve. Only the worthy could escape that fate.

sentences.zh: 況王鄴帥昧明哲之規，周太祖乃雄猜之主，欲無及禍，其可得乎！

translations.literal: How much more so for Military Governor Wang Ye, who was dim regarding policies of wise clarity—Zhou Taizu was a master both bold and suspicious; to wish to escape calamity, how could that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: How much more was this true of Wang Yin, who lacked prudent foresight, under Zhou Taizu, a ruler both formidable and suspicious—how could he hope to escape disaster!

sentences.zh: 自福進而下，皆將帥之英也，擁旌作翰，諒亦宜然。

translations.literal: From Fujin downward, all were heroes among generals and commanders; to bear banners and serve as frontier pillars was surely fitting for them as well.
translations.idiomatic: From Fujin onward, all were outstanding commanders; to bear imperial banners and serve as frontier pillars was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 惟彥超以捍寇而沒，可不謂忠乎！

translations.literal: Only Yanchao perished while resisting bandits—can this not be called loyal!
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanchao died holding the enemy at bay—can that be called anything but loyalty!
